compatibilityChanges: Subagent capacity moved from settings-injected values to host Volatile<number> fields; the science-result project/pair/pending fields are declared on the new inferred schema and the local settingsSource/dsh-settings injection seam was retired.
Tool results are first-class tool-role messages; toolCallId, isError and content are read from the message instead of a removed 'tool-result' content-block variant.
The catch-all 'plugin' message-source kind was removed upstream; the fork declares its science notice source kind locally through declaration merging.
Session format rose to V4; the fork migration test now expects session.v4.jsonl while the session.v2.jsonl predecessor remains the migration input.
Team member status simplified to running|inactive; the fork's assertions no longer expect an idle member state.
tools.restrict() now validates named tools against the live registry at call time; role allowlists continue to name only registered platform tools.
The external local-job Provider re-reads a job row after observing a released supervisor lock, closing a read-then-check window in which a committed terminal record could be reported as unknown.
Community README, dashboard, experiment layer and local checks remain; upstream release and administration workflows are not enabled.
platformFixes: first-loop analysis normalizes path separators before escape and evidence-link comparisons; POSIX-style prefix checks missed Windows relative paths.
Python subprocess helpers decode UTF-8 explicitly; the host locale default (GBK) broke several check scripts.
External-job and platform tests treat POSIX signal assertions as platform-specific; Node reports null exit signals on Windows.
Evidence collection records manifest paths with forward slashes on every host.
Test and build entry points resolve npm, pnpm and python3 through executable shims where the host lacks .exe aliases.

initialFailures.outcome: The scripted Agent run intermittently observed state 'unknown' after the worker finished all iterations. The provider observation read the job row before checking supervisor-lock ownership, so a terminal commit landing between the two reads was reported as lost ownership. The observation now re-reads the row after a released lock before declaring unknown; the full external-job suite passes.

cli-check rejected a deployment whose baseline still held the previous pin; updating the example deployment baseline to the new pin resolved it. The rejection itself confirmed the old-pin-refusal contract.
Manifest paths used OS separators, so the same file list differed on Windows. Manifest paths are now emitted as POSIX.

commands.scope: Full upstream host build and client project typecheck

documentationDiagnostics.explanation: The fork retains a local host extension and English community README, and omits upstream-owned workflows. Upstream generated catalogs do not incorporate the extension; pairing/link checks flag fork differences. Upstream prose/reference checks also reject existing community source and exact commit-based verification records. No gate was disabled or failure converted into success. Only the pinned-version references in the three community documents were revised; upstream-generated design/catalog documents and historical records were not rewritten.

limits: Windows verified locally; the POSIX-signal lifecycle assertions are skipped on this platform as designed. No macOS/Linux rerun and no real-model research run or scientific-quality evaluation.
Old deployment baseline must be explicitly updated. Keep Provider versions and original directories for unresolved operations.
No restoration of live Agent or experiment-controller authorization from disk.
Upstream product surfaces outside AI4Science integration are not exhaustively validated here.
Session format rose to V4 upstream; execution schema 2 unchanged and the existing v1 to v2 execution migration is retained.

recordUpgrade.note: The old-pin refusal was exercised directly: cli-check rejected a deployment carrying the previous baseline with a schema error before any migration. No dual-checkout record replay was rerun; session-format and execution-schema migration coverage comes from the platform suites.

commitHooks: Not run on this host; integration branch prepared in an isolated worktree.
